lesson.title: Buenos Días, Buenas Noches: Sunrise and Moonrise
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol wakes up with the sun every morning, and goes to sleep with the moon every night. Let's stretch awake and curl up asleep with Sol!
Stretch your arms up high like the sun is rising. Say [[buenos días]] — that means 'good morning'!
Now curl up small and close your eyes like the moon is rising. Say [[buenas noches]] — that means 'good night'!
You said buenos días for morning and buenas noches for night! Tomorrow, Sol needs your help remembering the magic words.

config.instructions: Match the Spanish greeting to its picture.

objectives: Say buenos días while acting out waking up, and buenas noches while acting out going to sleep
Match this week's greeting words to the right picture or action with support
materialsNeeded: A sun picture and a moon picture (drawn or printed)
Open space to stretch and curl up
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Hold up (or draw) a sun and say 'buenos días' — good morning. Stretch up tall together.
2. Hold up (or draw) a moon and say 'buenas noches' — good night. Curl up small together.
3. Play a quick sort: show the sun, child says buenos días and stretches; show the moon, child says buenas noches and curls up. Mix up the order to keep it playful.
4. Act it out as a mini-story: 'wake up' (buenos días, stretch), then later 'go to sleep' (buenas noches, curl up).
5. Complete the on-screen matching activity together, reading each tile aloud since your child may not read yet.
6. Close by asking: 'What do we say to the sun? What do we say to the moon?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: use real light in the house (a sunny window, a night-light) instead of pictures, so the sun/moon connection feels concrete
Ready for more: ask your child to add their own morning action (a big yawn) or night action (a pretend snore) to go with each phrase
Both phrases are long for a first echo — it's fine if your child only manages 'días' or 'noches' at first and grows into the full phrase over the week
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken and acted activity — success looks like the correct phrase paired with the correct action (stretch for buenos días, curl up for buenas noches), not a written answer. In the matching game: buenos días → ☀️, buenas noches → 🌙, hola → 👋, adiós → 🚶.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Continues the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 target by pairing two new greeting phrases with physical actions (TPR — Total Physical Response), the recommended method for this band's oral/aural-first design, and recycles hola/adiós from Day 1 in the matching activity.

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and do the action together.
